decisions.reason: Although it was no longer observed on the website after 2019, this underground loader line is close to the firm's core mining business and such heavy multi-model machinery is usually retained for several years unless demand clearly disappoints.

These underground dump trucks remain strategically aligned with the firm's underground and safety-focused equipment portfolio, so management would more likely continue than withdraw them despite some uncertainty from later website evidence.

A construction site dumper is less differentiated and less central to the firm's specialized underground and lifting strengths, making it the most likely recent launch to be discontinued if sales and margins were only moderate.
The inclined furniture lift line fits the firm's lifting and transport know-how and can benefit from service, parts and model variation, which argues for keeping it on the market.
The inclined building material lift line matches the company's focus on practical, safety-oriented equipment for demanding job sites and is likely to be kept as part of a broader lifting offering.

The truck-mounted inclined furniture lift is somewhat narrower and more specialized than the other lift products, but it still complements the firm's lifting portfolio enough that management would more likely retain it than exit immediately.
